_comment: Repo-relative paths that PERMANENTLY show up in `git status --porcelain` and must never count as evidence of a round's own uncommitted work, read by check_round_recorded.py's unattributed_dirty_paths (round 291, closing round 283's backlog item 3 — the git_committed-coverage gap). Two distinct sources so far: (1) state/round_counter, the shared bookkeeping file every round bumps early in its own run, so it is always ` M` mid-round by design (see feedback_check_for_concurrent_rounds); (2) the four files a wholly separate autonomous system (the Hermes gateway, see skills/session-inheritance-audit/SKILL.md's 'hermes-not-a-driver-process' pitfall) leaves permanently untracked under languages/whence/ — confirmed unchanged across dozens of rounds (152, 172, 198, 201, and every round since; most recently round 288/289/290). Add a new path here ONLY after independently confirming it recurs across multiple rounds' `git status` with no round ever attributing or committing it — a real one-off leftover diff belongs in git via `git add`+`git commit`, not in this allowlist.
_round_349_addendum: Round 349 (harness A) added the 13 paths above the original five, on the handoff round 348 left explicitly for this track ('the allowlist was deliberately NOT widened ... recorded as a next step for harness(A)/skills(B), which own that checker'). The bar the _comment sets is met: the Hermes gateway wrote all 13 at 23:32-23:42 UTC on 2026-08-29, round 348 inspected them mid-round and attributed them to that system in its own knowledge file section 7, and round 349 independently re-confirmed the same authorship fingerprint before adding them here. No round has ever committed or claimed any of them. Adding them takes the record-gap check's unattributed-path count from 27 to 1. TWO deliberate exclusions, both TRACKED files the same system modified: languages/whence/SECURITY.md and CLAUDE.md. This registry models UNTRACKED leftovers only -- a separate system editing a TRACKED file is a different class (round 348's own words), and allowlisting one would mean 'never look at this diff again', which is the wrong answer for both. CLAUDE.md was committed by round 349 with attribution. SECURITY.md is escalated to the operator unresolved -- see round 349's knowledge file; its rewrite asserts four security controls that do not exist in this repo.
_round_441_addendum: Round 441 (skills B) added ONE path, languages/whence/examples/agi_buy_and_hold.lang -- the FIFTEENTH program the Hermes gateway has left in that directory, written 2026-09-01 23:12:22 UTC while round 440 was running and reported by round 440 (knowledge/round-440-*, next-step 4). It was added HERE ONLY and deliberately NOT to .gitignore -- round 444 added the .gitignore line, in the commit that declared the file in the new membership roster, which is what this addendum's last sentence asked for. Round 441 measured the difference rather than assuming it: `curecheck.field_corpus_drift()` shells out to `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard examples`, so an ignore line is read by that drift detector too. With the line in force (tested via .git/info/exclude, restored byte-identically, md5 036208b4a1ab4a235d75c181e685e5a3), drift goes (['agi_buy_and_hold.lang'], []) -> ([], []), the census still declares 14, the file is still on disk, and languages/whence/tests/test_field_corpus_selector.py::test_the_live_tree_has_no_drift goes RED -> GREEN. That is a live finding silenced, not attributed. This registry has no second reader: nothing outside check_round_recorded.py reads it, so an entry here suppresses the record-gap report and leaves the drift red. Round 402's fourteen ignore lines were NOT this mistake -- the census already named all fourteen when they landed, so `untracked - declared` was empty either way. The rule that falls out: an ignore line for a foreign artefact may land in the same commit as its census entry or after it, never before. Whoever re-makes the census (round 440 next-step 4) should add the .gitignore line THEN, in that commit, and delete this addendum's second sentence.
_round_444_addendum: Round 444 (language C) carried out this addendum's last sentence and closed round 440's next-step 4. The census was NOT re-made: state/whence/round-384/field-names.json is EVIDENCE (whence/foreign.py's FOREIGN_NAMES entry rule (a) cites it by path, so re-taking it retroactively rewrites the reason each entry exists) and it was ALSO the selector, which is a live question. A new file, state/whence/round-444/field-roster.json, is the membership and declares fifteen; curecheck.field_roster_names() reads it and curecheck.frozen_census() reads the census. field_corpus_drift() then went (['agi_buy_and_hold.lang'], []) -> ([], []) BY DECLARATION, before any .gitignore line existed -- measured, not assumed -- and the .gitignore line landed in the same commit, after. tests/test_field_corpus_selector.py::test_the_live_tree_has_no_drift is green again for the honest reason. agi_buy_and_hold.lang stays in the paths list above for the same reason its fourteen siblings do.
